explanation: An Elamite king carried the stele off as war booty to Susa, in modern Iran, where French archaeologists dug it up in 1901. Its laws set penalties by social class.

claims.text: Hammurabi, king of Babylon in the 1700s BC, had his code of laws inscribed on a stone stele.
The Code of Hammurabi has about 280 laws (282 in the modern numbering).
Nebuchadnezzar II ruled Babylon in the 500s BC, Sargon of Akkad ruled in the 2300s BC, and Ashurbanipal was a king of Assyria in the 600s BC.
An Elamite king took the stele to Susa as plunder.
French archaeologists found the stele at Susa, in modern Iran, in 1901.
Penalties in the Code of Hammurabi varied with the social class of those involved.
